title: Bodybuilding cuisine: Idiot proof fried rice recipe
summary: NH cooks his staple egg-heavy fried rice on camera: an egg-chunk base, day-old rice, more eggs cracked on top, seasoning, an optional lean protein, and olive oil at the end. He presents it as a cheap, nutritious, hard-to-ruin bulk meal that keeps a week in the fridge, and defends salting home-cooked food generously for people who train.
claims: His fried rice uses only cheap, simple ingredients (eggs, white rice, salt, olive oil) yet is very nutritious and tasty
Start with olive oil and 4-5 eggs cooked until the white is only just set; these become the chewy egg chunks, so don't overcook them because they keep cooking the whole time
Break the eggs when the whites have set but the yolks are still runny so yolk and white mix into the chunks
Use rice cooked 1-2 days earlier and kept in the fridge for a firmer texture; fresh rice absorbs more moisture and comes out softer, but it is easier for beginners
Thai rice is best for fried rice; jasmine rice is too rigid and sticky rice turns it into goo because the eggs already provide the stickiness
Crack 3-6 more eggs over the rice and mix so the yolk soaks into every grain; if the mix gets too liquid, add more rice to soak up the moisture
Fried rice keeps 7-9 days in the fridge, so cook a big batch
Cook the eggs on low heat at first, then turn the heat up once the top eggs are in; there is too much moisture for it to burn, which is why the recipe is idiot proof
Keep turning the rice from the bottom so it dries evenly without burning; cooking ends when the grains are dry and separate
Season generously with salt, onion powder and garlic powder; skip pepper
People who train need sodium for muscle contraction and water retention in the muscle; sodium is not the enemy, inactivity is, though you should get your blood pressure checked
Supermarket food has about 5 times the sodium of his home-cooked rice, so don't be shy salting your own cooking
Add a small amount of lean protein (chicken breast, shrimp, lean ham, veggie sausages); avoid beef and fatty pork because they make it too rich
Finish with olive oil until the grains glisten, then cut the heat right away so the oil is absorbed rather than cooked
Serve it with a light cabbage salad to offset a heavy meal
Rice is a good carb source, but plain white rice every day gets boring; fried rice keeps it palatable
